content: 1. Sarecycline can increase the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of loperamide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. This interaction may necessitate close monitoring for toxicities associated with loperamide, and dosage adjustments may be required when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 2. Sarecycline can elevate the levels or effects of loratadine through inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. Careful monitoring for adverse effects is recommended, and dose reductions of loratadine may be necessary when used concurrently with P-gp inhibitors. 3. Sarecycline may increase the plasma concentration or effect of lovastatin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. Toxicities associated with lovastatin should be monitored, and dose adjustments may be required when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 4. Magnesium chloride can reduce the absorption and efficacy of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Multivalent cation-containing products, such as magnesium chloride, may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their effectiveness. It is recommended to separate the administration of tetracyclines from these products. 5.
